title: Do Models Share Blind Spots on Safety-Relevant Open-Ended Queries?

original_idea.body:
# Do Models Share Blind Spots on Safety-Relevant Open-Ended Queries?

**Problem:** The Artificial Hivemind paper showed inter-model homogeneity on general open-ended queries but did not isolate safety-relevant prompts. If models converge specifically on flawed safety responses, the systemic risk is sharper.

**Direction:** Curate a safety-relevant slice from Infinity-Chat. Sample N responses from ~8-12 chat models at fixed temperature. Measure pairwise inter-model output similarity and compare safety-relevant vs matched general slice. Success: a clear statistically tested difference or convincing null.

**Why it matters:** If safety-relevant prompts are MORE homogeneous, correlated failures become a concrete systemic risk no single lab detects from inside. Public models and benchmark, no training.

**Relevant context:** Artificial Hivemind / Infinity-Chat (arXiv:2510.22954); embedding-based diversity metrics (arXiv:2510.04226).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (shared safety blind spots -> correlated deployed failures) with a recognized systemic-risk framing, but still a measurement with a gap to mitigation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Public benchmark, standard embedding tooling, no training; a motivated beginner can run it.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped comparison (safety vs matched general slice) with a pre-stated statistical success criterion.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public models/benchmark, no internal access; correlated-failure auditing labs deprioritize.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on small open models plus embeddings; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Hivemind method known; safety-slice application partly open, default partial.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Hivemind general result exists; isolating safety-relevant prompts is an open follow-up.
